chapters.html:
Of course Mydei would find him sitting at the edge of the Dome of the Stars.

He had joined the feast with the other Chrysos Heirs with a smile on his face, one that screamed fake! Please don’t talk to me! but Mydei suspected it was only out of necessity. Aglaea and Anaxa had been the ones to send out invites, and the pair had practically raised Phainon. The last thing he’d do was refuse.

But once the event was over, Phainon must have bolted out of the room almost immediately because the minute Mydei turned after stacking the plates the white haired man was gone. He had sighed, and raised a questioning brow to Aglaea, who pointed towards the entrance leading to the Dome. Before he left, she gently grabbed his wrist to get his attention.

“Be gentle,” she whispered, teal eyes focused intently on his own, “you know that out of all of us, he’s the one having a hard time adjusting. His mental state is going to take some time to fix, and I’ve already asked Hyacine to help him out. I know you two are close as ever, but it’s just a small reminder.”

Mydei thanked her, and made a quick stop to the kitchen to make two mugs of hot chocolate–Phainon’s comfort drink and the very first one he himself had after stepping into Okhema thanks to none other than the Deliverer. Of course a hot beverage definitely wouldn’t solve everything right away, but hey, he was willing to do anything to help his partner. Oh, and while also making sure he doesn’t set him off in the process. The fact he had even showed up to the banquet meant he wanted to make an effort, albeit reluctantly. 

Oh, and he also ran to his room to grab a quick something and tucked it safely into his pocket, giving it a few pats before heading out.

The sanctuary Cyrene and Caelus made for them was beautiful. Covered in shades of pale lilac and pink with little hints of pastel yellow and turquoise made the whole place pleasant to look at. At first glance, anyone could tell it was meant to resemble the Garden of Life–one of the more peaceful and tranquil areas of Okhema, compared to the bustling streets of Mamoreal Market. There were only two striking differences–one of them being the absence of the Dawn Device, for in its place was an actual sun. It was still an artificial star since they were living in the literal book Caelus and Cyrene had used to record Amphoreus’ memories, but real nonetheless. It had been surreal at first, watching the sun dip below the horizon and give way to the moon, bathing the Sunlit Garden in a comforting darkness so different from the harsh, suffocating black he had faced in the Sea of Souls. That very first night, he left his curtains open, letting the moonlight spill into his room. And for the first time in a long while, he slept without nightmares.

That was the first difference. The second?

“Found you,” Mydei smiled, sitting next to Phainon and setting the mugs down. The Dome of the Stars was the only part of the Exotale that was connected to the real world. From here, they could see the numerous stars littered across the expanse of the universe, some shining brightly and others fizzing and dying out as they go through the constant cycle of life and rebirth. And in the center of it all, shrouded in dust and glowing a magnificent yellow was where Amphoreus would be reborn into a proper planet, free from the reins of Zandar and Iron Tomb. 

He wondered how Amphoreus would look once the planet finally materializes–would all the city states be there? Would they be in ruins or restored to their former glory? When he had asked Caelus during one of his trips he shrugged and said he and the Genius’ had no clue. They had the data and memories to re–weave everything back into order, so even if Amphoreus turned out to be a barren wasteland they had the power of Remembrance. 

However, that process was going to take a long time, and Mydei, who always looked into the future knew he didn’t exactly have a ‘long time.’ A long time to do something he had been wanting to do for quite some time.

But first, there was one person he needed to beat some sense into. Figuratively speaking.

Phainon huffed, bowing his head down, his white hair curtaining his face. “I thought it was supposed to be me chasing you all the time, not the other way around.”

His voice sounded rough, coarse. Mydei frowned but chose not to comment on it for now. Instead he chose the old and familiar route since that was the only way to get any sort of reaction out of him. “Decided we needed a change of pace. After all, I can't have our patient running around on his grandpa legs now, can I?”

He smirked, and as expected the man sat up straight and looked at him in pure disbelief, hands suspended mid-air and eyes blown wide. “I am sorry!?” he shrieked, and yep, his voice was now mysteriously back to normal. “I may be older both physically and mentally and literally but that does not give you the right to call me grandpa!”

“Sure. Grandpa.”

Phainon snarled, rage in his eyes. For a split second Mydei thought he saw his eyes flash gold before whatever rage had entered his body fade away, shoulders sagging as his gaze fixated on the stars once again. “Whatever Mydei. Just…get to the point. Otherwise leave me be, please.”

The way he choked on the last word, nearly implausible that he had strained his ears stirred something inside him. This wasn't the first time Mydei had seen him broken–back in every cycle Phainon had moments where his emotions dictated his actions, most of the time being on the battlefield. Sometimes they slip through the cracks when they sparred, followed by a few minutes of him reigning his madness in before they continued. Mydei always ended them and dragged him to the baths so they could cool down.

Phainon had worn his heart on his sleeve, yes, but what no one knew was how real those feelings actually were. Not even Mydei himself.

And now armed with the knowledge of what happened in every recurrence…

“Silent, aren't we? Got nothing to say, Your Highness?”

The bitterness in his voice caught him off guard. Mydei raised a brow. “I didn’t say such a thing. I’m just gathering my thoughts.”

“Right.” Phainon laughed bitterly. “Just gathering your thoughts. “Something that you’ve never done in any cycle if I may remind you.”

“What are you talking about?” Mydei snapped, irritation buzzing in his chest that he swiftly tampered down. Right. He had to remind himself he had to be the mature one between them. For Phainon’s sake.

If he had to be patient, then he’d be goddamn patient. All for him. 

So he took one of the mugs and shoved it into Phainon’s hands before the white–haired man could utter another annoying half-retort, smirking when his jaw slackened as he saw what was inside. “Did you…make this,” he asked softly, almost in disbelief. Mydei didn’t know if he wanted to laugh or cry at the amount of emotions he was going through all in the span of five minutes. He claimed he couldn’t feel anything anymore and yet here he was, looking so small and fragile and wondering why he was even here. Wondering why he was here. Wondering why everyone remembered him, the Nameless Hero who was supposed to be forgotten by all. Wondering what he did to deserve this when all he wanted was to be alone in his room, curled under the sheets and crying himself to sleep.

It made Mydei want to throw up.

He nodded, grabbing his own cup. “Drink it before it gets cold, otherwise you won’t stop complaining about how bitter it tastes.”

Phainon scowled, grumbling something into his cup as he took small sips, not noticing the small, genuine smile on Mydei’s face. ‘Good,’ he thought. ‘At least he didn’t refuse. That’s a good sign.’ But that didn’t mean he would push. Baby steps. This was one battle where rushing in would end in catastrophic disaster. 

This was a bit weird. Back when they penned their final words Phainon sounded and acted normal, even throwing teasing jabs at him when it had been his turn. He definitely didn't sound like he had been hiding anything either. So where did this sudden self-hatred come from? Was it because of the memories? 

Phainon exhaled tiredly, swirling the mug around, the frown never leaving his face. His mouth moved, muttering something that he couldn’t quite understand. “What?” Mydei asked, scooting a bit closer but maintaining a respectable distance.”

“Why?” he rasped, voice sounding hoarse despite finishing half of his drink. “Why are you here trying to do…whatever it is that you’re doing?”

‘Because I care, you idiot!’ Mydei wanted to yell. “Because I want to, you doofus. Is it hard to believe that people care about you?”

“They shouldn’t,” he whispered, holding the mug so tight it might break under his fingers. “None of you should be anywhere near me.”

“And who are you to say that?” Mydei asked, and immediately back tracked when he mentally replayed Caelus’ words from a few days ago.

“He still blames himself,” he said sadly as the two watched Phainon from a distance. “His rage and fury are all gone, but because it’s gone he’s left with nothing. Herta said you can compare him to an empty shell–completely hollowed out.”

“And there’s no saying when he’ll be back to normal?” Mydei asked, clawed fingers sinking into his flesh, though not deep enough to break through the skin. 

Caelus paused, chewing his lip before looking directly into his eyes and said, “I’m not sure he’ll ever be back to normal. His mental state is, to put it bluntly, a mess. A huge mess caused by the Eternal Recurrences. Killing all of you guys over and over has made him numb. Sometimes the spark’s in his eyes when he’s around his parents, but you guys…”

He put his hands out and waved them frantically. “I’m not blaming you guys or accusing you of anything! But you gotta understand no matter how hard he tries to be around you all, he just…can’t. All I can say is give him space, but also make him feel included. Don’t lash out. Let him come out of his shell slowly.”

And Mydei had just broken that rule. 

Phainon was immediately on him, tossing the mug aside and pinned him to the ground, Dawnmaker in his right hand. The sound of the porcelain shattering reverberated through the empty space, filling his ears. Those cerulean blue eyes were wild, angry, almost feral. “What did you just say?” he asked in a low, threatening voice. His hand that was gripping Dawnmaker was shaking violently. “Say it again Mydei. I dare you to.”

Now Mydei wasn’t that good with words, despite popular belief. Sure, he was good at giving speeches, arguing with the Council and talking to children, but that was about it.  Comforting people was not his forte, no matter how hard he tried. Lady Tribbie had helped him when he and the detachment first came to Okhema, months before the fated duel between him and his father but no matter how hard he tried and followed their instructions, his voice always stayed rough and hard. It wasn’t the words itself, but rather his tone. 

For fuck sake he was a Kremnoan. Their prince for crying out loud! His people were famous for being rough and everyone knew that. Being soft was a foreign concept, and that was most certainly not because of any random code. But looking at Phainon now, so close to snapping and doing something that’ll harm him more than Mydei himself, maybe, just maybe he needed to be rough. Rough, but also calm. He had to be the bigger one between them now. Phainon had always shouldered their burden in every cycle, shouldering the knowledge of Amphoreus’ true purpose all alone. The worst part right now was that Cyrene was no longer alive, sacrificing herself so that all of them could be reborn in the near future. If only she were here, she’d know what to do.

But she wasn’t here and he was, and he was not abandoning him. Not now, not ever.

Mydei gulped, calming his pounding heart. He no longer has his curse, so he had to tread carefully. But saying anything else would easily trigger him too, so for now it was best to go with Phainon’s flow.

So he steeled his resolve, met his gaze head on, and said, “You heard me. Who are you to say you’re endangering us just by standing near us?”

Phainon’s breathing hitched, staring at him like he had just slapped him. His eyes flashed gold once again for a few seconds before he snarled and placed Dawnmaker right above his throat, its tip gleaming under the light of the countless stars. “You don’t get to say that,” he hissed.

Mydei raised a brow, praying to Nikador that Phainon couldn’t sense his fear. “Then who does?” he argued. “Do you think any of us are happy to see you distancing yourself from us Deliverer? Do you think we’re celebrating behind your back and avoiding you because of what you’ve done? I know sometimes you’re stupid, but I never thought you’d be this dense!”

“SHUT UP!” Phainon screamed so loud, people in the Sunlit Garden would’ve heard him. Dawnmaker was dangerously close to his neck. His breathing became erratic. “Shut up,” he said again, lips trembling and tears starting to form in the corner of his eyes. “You don’t get to say that. No one here gets to say that! None of you understand what me and Cyrene went through, and just because all of you have all your memories back doesn’t mean you can understand the sheer pain and agony I had to endure to get all of us to this point.”

“Then make us understand,” Mydei said softly, grabbing Dawnmaker. He hissed in slight pain as the sharp blade cut through skin, red blood seeping through and dripping to the ground. Phainon gasped, his expression shifting from anger to fear quickly it made Mydei want to laugh. Emotionally numb? Him?

“Let go,” came Phainon’s voice, hollow. Mydei shook his head, only gripping Dawnmaker more tightly. He started to get frustrated all over again. “Mydei, seriously let go. You’re bleeding, and you’re not immortal anymore.”

“It’s nothing Hyacine can’t fix,” Mydei replied casually, suppressing a wince–the pain was starting to get to him a little, and he had high pain tolerance. “Pain is secondary compared to what you’re going through right now. I can handle it.”

Phainon looked at him like he was insane. He probably was. Or maybe he was delirious from the blood loss, in which case he should go seek out Hyacine, but how could he when Phainon needed someone with him right now before he combust? How could he leave him alone for even a second in the state he was in? 

But…he should probably take Phainon’s advice and let Dawnmaker go lest his small wound get serious and require urgent medical attention. Hyacine definitely wouldn’t be happy.

“You’re insane,” Phainon muttered, Dawnmaker disappearing in a flurry of sparkles. He stood up, only to flop down next to him with an unreadable expression on his face. “You’re actually insane to do that when you’re not wearing your gauntlets. What even possessed you to do such a thing?”

Mydei sat up and shrugged. “Do I need a reason? I care.”

“You shouldn’t.”

“Well, I do, and there’s nothing you can do.”

“Not even if I bribe you?”

“Are you really going to stoop that low Deliverer?”

“Would it be that unbelievable if I said I would if it meant making sure you’d all be safe?” 

“For the last time,” Mydei said as slow as possible, trying very hard not to throttle the idiot’s throat, “I don’t care about all that. I only care about you. You, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae.”

“And I’m saying you shouldn’t,” Phainon said again, looking away. His snowy white hair curtained his eyes. He kept clenching his fists. “You’re all wasting your time on me Mydei. Can’t you see I’m broken? Broken beyond repair both physically and mentally?”

Broken. A word Dan Heng and Hyacine once used to describe him right after they had all settled in properly. The way he flinched at every little noise. How he was always standing three feet away from everyone and refused to take even a small step closer. His body and mind were still processing that it was all over and that he could rest. It was like he was actively looking for a reason to kill. And here Mydei thought he’d be the hardest one to control, having fought the black tide over and over with no breaks in between.

But no one saw him like that. In Mydei’s eyes he was the same Deliverer who fought him for 10 days and nights straight until they both collapsed from exhaustion. The same person who cracked jokes all day and dragged his ass to the baths twice a day. The same guy who accidentally set the Chrysos Heir’s kitchen on fire during his first day in Okhema because he didn’t know how to work the electrical stove until he taught him, and made him a Fasolada as a thank you gift.

He might be broken, but he was still human, and what he needed was help. Something Phainon thought he didn’t deserve. 

“Yes, you are broken,” Mydei started to say slowly, carefully watching Phainon’s reaction. “But that doesn’t mean you aren’t fixable. Your brain doesn’t want you to believe it because of everything you experienced. You suffered alone, and you couldn’t reach out and tell anyone, not even Cyrene because you had to kill her at the beginning of each cycle so she could recount the stories to the Demiurge core.”

Phainon opened his mouth but he held up a finger. “I’m not done yet. I think what you need is someone to remind you constantly that this is real. That you are real. Tell me, what do you see right now?”

Phainon’s nose scrunched, giving him a weird, almost judgemental look, and all he did was raise a brow in response, telling him he was serious. He sighed, the remaining fight draining from his body. “Fine, I’ll play your little game if it’ll get you to leave.”

Mydei smiled. “Good. Now, answer.”

“What can I see, huh? Well, you for starters. Then the translucent blue dome beneath our feet, the stars in the sky and that huge galaxy. Then…the entrance to the building.”

“Ok. Now then, what can you feel?”

“...What?” Phainon looked frustrated again. “Mydei,” he growled, fists clenching once again, “what game are you playing right now? What’s the purpose of this?”

“Just answer. You’ll figure out the answer yourself,” was all Mydei said.

Phainon looked like he wanted to storm out of there and lock himself in his room. Too bad Mydei could pin him in his place. He had no way to escape. And Phainon knew that too.

“...Fine. I can feel the artificial wind blowing my hair gently, the coolness of the floor, your breath in my ear…yeah that's all.”

“That’s good. Now, what can you hear?”

“The breeze, your voice, the stars twinkling, the music…Cyrene…”

Mydei frowned but didn’t say anything, instead shelving that comment for later to bring up with Hyacine. “Ok,” he said once he realized Phainon was done. “That’s all the questions I want to ask.”

Phainon looked at him confused. Rightfully so. “That’s it? I don’t get it.”

‘Well, you answered everything that you felt. That you saw. That you heard,” Mydei explained. “You kept saying your brain kept telling you that none of this is real. Now that you’ve listed everything out loud, what do you think now? Still believe all this is fake?”

The man opened and closed his mouth a bunch of times, the gears in his head working hard, probably trying to refute his point. Well, how could he?

Then, in a weak voice he protested, “It–it isn’t that simple Mydei.”

Mydei’s smirked softened, and he opened his arms, a silent invitation. “I know. But you have to start somewhere, right? So let’s start here. Please?”

Of course Mydei knew things would never be simple anymore. Since when were things ever simple? But that didn’t mean they couldn’t try to mend things. All he had to do was nudge his partner in the right direction. 

Phainon looked at him, and then at arms, hesitated for a few seconds before crawling slowly towards him and laid his head on his chest. But he still maintained some amount of distance out of…respect? To which Mydei scoffed under his breath and wrapped his arms around him and pulled him close. The tiny squeak made him chuckle. “Relax a little. You're stiff under my arms.”

“I’m…trying.” Phainon curled up closer, his breathing somewhat erratic but calm. “It’s hard to…relax.”

“I know.” Mydei rocked them back and forth. “But all I’m asking is for you to try instead of shutting yourself out. Take that first step please. We’ll be there with you. You aren’t alone. Everyone’s worried about you, you know that? We all want you to get better and have you return to your normal self.

“They are?” Phainon asked in a small voice, looking at him with wide eyes akin to a child. Blue eyes were shining with unshed tears.

He nodded. “Of course they are. You honestly think they want to let you go? They’ve been waiting for the day you’d talk to them. They’re patient, all of them, giving you space.”

All of them had spent time after work and meals, discussing about Phainon and how to help him. Hyacine and Anaxa mentioned he’d wander into their work area, lean against the wall and stare into a void like a statue until one of them nudged his shoulder gently. He’d shake his head, looking around and back at them in nervousness before retreating, muttering “I’m so sorry, I didn’t mean to.” Hysilens and Cerydra said they saw him idly watching the stars, and Castorice mentioned he’d help her, Tribbie and her sisters watch the Chimera’s without talking to them. Aglaea mourned the loss of the child she had brought back to Okhema after the black tide razed Aedes Elysiae and raised.

They all wanted him to come back. Maybe not back to normal, but back to some semblance of normalcy.

“But why?” Phainon’s voice cracked. The tears started to slowly trickle. “Why do they care? After all that–”

“Because we see you Phainon,” Mydei gently interrupted him, placing a finger on his lips. This was his chance. “We understand your pain because now we’ve seen it. Of course we’d be concerned. Aglaea keeps rambling about ways to crack your shell, and all Anaxa can do is watch her helplessly. Hyacine cries herself to sleep every night thinking of a cure, and Castorice makes plushies of you everyday as a mini shrine to get your attention–”

“Mydei,” Phainon said feebly.

“Cipher thinks of pranks that’d cheer you up. Heck, even Imperator Cerydra and Hysilens are worried about your well–being.”

“Mydei–”

“I’m not done. All I’m saying is that no one has ever given up on you. Our only goal is for you to get better and–”

“Mydei!”

Mydei stopped, teeth clenching tight as Phainon’s voice rang in his ears, loud and raw. Suddenly, he started to worry if he had stepped over the line, and Aglaea’s warning rang through his mind. 

But then he looked at the Deliverer’s face, and saw that familiar bright smile on his face, albeit a bit wobbly because he was ugly crying at this point. He sniffed, laughing wetly and nuzzled his head back into the crook of his neck. “You–you– Ok, ok ok ok ok ok ok ok. Ok. I think I get you now Mydei.”

“Do you though? Truly?” Mydei asked, cradling the back of his head.

“Kind of. Not fully really, but I think I can start to believe everyone isn’t comforting me out of duty or pity. That you really want me to feel better. Is that ok? Understanding all that for now?”

Mydei let the smile grow and nodded. “Of course.”

And for a while they just sat there, holding each other and not saying anything. Phainon apologized for breaking the mug and wasting all that lovely hot chocolate, to which Mydei shushed him and said it wasn’t his fault. He went quiet and the silence continued–this time like a comfortable blanket draping over them.

Phainon started to hum a low tune under his breath. A tune Mydei instantly recognized–the lullaby his mother sang to him every night. A tune Mydei found Phainon humming when they were in the baths or watching Okhema from the rooftops. It’s a song the man had come to associate with his partner. He let his eyes droop shut and relaxed.

The stars twinkled, and the galaxy in the middle of it all swirled in a continuous rhythm. The non–existent breeze played with their already messy hair. After a very long time things finally felt peaceful. That everything was finally falling into order. Just as how things should have always been. 

Huh.

Maybe Peucesta was right and he’d make a good bard. Minus the singing.

And there was one more thing on his mind as well. Something he had been wanting to ask Phainon but never really got the chance to.

“Hey, Phainon?”

“Hm?”

“Can you…can you shift into your other form? I mean, your eyes glowed gold a few times…”

“Oh, that?” Phainon hesitated, pulling back and placing a hand on his chin. “Well, I don’t want to say it’s complicated, but long story short kind of….I mean, my wings and halo have lost their shimmer and I still feel the phantom pain of the numerous scars. Professor Anaxa and Hyacine have been helping me to get rid of it so I can shift freely. But it’s strange. All of you have lost your powers and yet I haven’t…but in hindsight it does make sense,” he ended with a sigh.

Right. Because all their abilities had been strings of code. In Phainon’s case, because of his actions and the numerous Coreflames he had housed in his chest his body was permanently fractured. Granted he could hide it beneath all his layers, but the amount of scar tissue was something that couldn’t be fixed. Maybe for the time being, but so far, nothing was certain.

Phainon frowned, looking up. “Want me to try and change now? I promise it doesn’t hurt as before and I won’t rip my heart out. Now that you brought that up, I do want to test the waters a bit.” 

“...Only if it doesn’t hurt.” As much as Mydei wanted to scream no and shut down the idea, he couldn’t stop the curious feeling in him. He only saw his other form through his memories of the recurrences–the two large and beautiful asymmetrical wings that protruded from his back, causing a huge crack to run down his spine, coalesced blood spiking out from his porcelain skin. The two halos that floated behind his head, the inner one being the symbol of Kephale. Dawnmaker, enlarged and floating beneath his palm with a deadly gleam. He had died countless times by that sword, and he had openly admitted he’d gladly die countless more. He cleared his throat and leaned back, giving Phainon some space. “I trust that you know your limits.”

“Don’t worry,” Phainon chirped cheerfully, giving him a thumbs up. “I’m certain I’ll be able to do it. Oh, but just a heads up, I’ll have to jump down the platform to transform. I’ve heard from Caelus the air around me tends to get a little heated if you know what I mean.”

“Do whatever you want,” he grunted out, getting up and stepping back. “As long as you make sure you don’t do anything stupid and hurt yoursel–.”

Wait a second, did he just say he was going to jump??

“Phainon!?” Mydei shrieked.

“I’ll be fine!” the idiot man shouted back, standing up. And then tipped over the platform and plunged to his death.

“Phainon!!” Mydei screamed, staring at where he had been standing just a second earlier in pure horror and bolted to the edge, searching for any sign of the moron, heart pounding when he couldn’t see anything shining. He…he didn’t just plummet to his death, did he? They couldn’t die here even if they tried. But they still didn’t know much about this place. 

Oh Nikador, what was he going to say to his parents? That his son foolishly tried to do something and now he might not appear again unless Caelus rewrites him back into existence? Could that even be done?? And it wasn’t like the Trailblazer could just pop in at random time. Ok maybe he could but that was beside the point. And who knew when he’d show up. And that’s all with the belief Caelus could bring him back to life. Oh Titans he felt sick. 

However just when he was about to run back to get Aglaea he saw a flash of gold and indigo, small and brief but it was there, and the next thing he saw was his partner in the air, wings large and impressive as always, sending small gusts of wind everywhere and halo glowing dimly behind him. His hair was once again a light gold, longer and flowing with the wind. Molten gold eyes slowly opened and it was now that he noticed what Phainon had meant when he said his World Bearer form lost it’s lustre.

The blood that he could see through the cracks no longer sparkled as they had in the past. His body, which had this waxy look to it, had dulled. Really dulled. Dulled down to the point that the tattoo that ran across his chest and collarbone was the only thing standing out apart from the bronze choker. The tear tracks on his face had all but evaporated.

The Coreflames that once sustained him and kept his body nourished were gone, and its effects were noticeable.

Phainon turned halfway, and his left hand extended towards the sky, illuminated by the stars. His whole body was glowing thanks to them. Mydei felt his breathing hitch at the sight. But what was he doing? His body language looked…off. There was no other way to put it

“Phainon?” Mydei asked, stepping forward.

“The stars Mydei,” the man whispered, clenching his fingers. He had to strain his ears to hear what he was saying. “From up here, the stars seem so much closer. I feel like I can hold them in my palm and cradle their warmth.”

He gave his wings a few hard flaps before turning to smile at Mydei and flew back down, hovering before him. He opened his palm to reveal a tiny light, the smile never leaving his face. Mydei didn’t stop the small gasp that escaped his lips.

“Put your hands together like mine,” Phainon said, using his free hand to adjust his posture. Then, with the care that one wouldn’t associate with an Emanator of Destruction, he deposited the tiny star into his open palms.

Mydei half expected it to burn in his palm; after all, he was holding a literal star. But to his surprise, it didn’t. Instead, it was warm–a gentle, comforting heat that wrapped around him like an embrace on a cold, stormy night. The warmth seeped into his skin, and when he gave it a careful prod, the star burst softly, sending stardust scattering through the air. He let out a quiet, breathless ah, equal parts awe and wonder.

“Surprised?” Phainon asked. “I had to alleviate the scorching fire in my soul. What better way to do it than make small stars?”

“So you….you're actually–”

He smiled, cupping his cheek. “Yes Mydei, I'm slowly healing. The heat searing my body from the inside out should hopefully be gone soon. And by soon I don’t mean within a few days. I’d say around the time Amphoreus becomes a planet. And as for how long I’ve been doing this”–he gestured at the stars–“it hasn’t been that long. In actuality it was Professor Anaxa’s idea after he asked me to visit him to check my body–that was the only time I’ve ever spoken to him or anyone by the way. He and Lady Tribbie thought that maybe if I started to expel the energy in small amounts I should be free from the scorching heat. How do I feel under your arms?”

Now that he mentioned it, he felt warm, but not like he was holding a literal sun, but rather a nice and cozy bonfire. And it was now that he noticed how cold the Dome was and felt a shiver down his spine. Phainon chuckled and landed, feet hitting the floor and let Mydei hug him properly.

“Warm,” he said, plopping his head on Phainon’s shoulder. “Not unbearably hot but a gentle warmth, like I’m sitting in front of a campfire. You really are getting better in your own way, aren’t you?”

Mydei felt Phainon nod. “Yeah. Yeah, I am. Yet for some reason I can’t believe it. I can’t believe I’m here, healing, standing in front of you. It’s probably gonna take me some time to get used to it,” he admitted shyly.

“And I’ll tell you over and over that it’s all ok.” Mydei pulled back. “Take as long as you need. Don’t they say healing isn’t linear?”

Phainon chuckled. “That’s what Hyacine and the healers at the Twilight Courtyard say all the time.”

“If they say it, then you know it’s correct.”

“They are the professionals. Who am I to argue with their logic?”

“Even so, I don’t think you need to be a medical professional to know that.”

“Well, fuck you.”

Mydei smirked. “Getting petty now, are we?”

“...Fuck you again.”

“You’re getting sloppy with your responses, Deliverer.”

“Shut. Up!”

“You’re proving my point.”

“You’re so insufferable,” Phainon groaned, now resting his head on Mydei’s shoulder. “Makes me wonder who died and made you king. Must you always be so bossy?”

Mydei laughed, patting the back of his head. “How do you think I’ve lasted this long as Kremnos’ leader?”

“Being an asshole,” came his murmured answer. Mydei rolled his eyes. “Your words, not mine.”

“You’re the worst,” Phainon muttered, and a small kiss was placed on the side of his neck. “But you are the person I fell for in every cycle.”

“Now I’m wondering who fell for who first the most. Though this may be a question we might never get a proper answer to unless we count a few million times,” Mydei joked.

Phainon scoffed. “Cowering already? I bet I can go through all 33,550,336 cycles worth of memories and get the answer in a few minutes.”

“Oh really?” Now this was what Mydei had sorely missed. The competitive side of him. “Just because you remember everything before us isn’t an advantage, Deliverer. Remember who always won the book sorting contests at the library?”

“I’ve gotten better these days. But then again, who’s to say we won’t tie?”

Mydei grimaced. Right, more than winning the two always somehow managed to finish tasks right at the same time. On those days he wondered if the universe had it out for him. But they always made up for it through other weird and wacky contest ideas, like who could run around Okhema the fastest, or who could tame the most Chimeras.

Silly? Yes? But fun?

Oh, they enjoyed it.

Another small kiss was pressed to his neck. “Now you’re thinking too much. C’mon, relax a little. Loosen up! The night is still young.”

“Using my words against me I see.”

“I can tell you’re proud.”

Mydei smiled. “I am.”

Phainon leaned back slightly to look at his face and beamed, eyes crinkled at the corners. “Thank you. For all this.” He shuffled around a bit. “I think those words are finally starting to register in my brain.”

“That’s good.” He dropped a kiss on his forehead. “I’m glad you’re taking that first step now.”

“I mean, I took that step a while ago–”

“HKS. You know what I mean,” Myei mock scolded. 

Phainon laughed. “Yeah yeah.” He gave him another tight hug. “I know De. I know. And this time we’ll–”

“Yip! Yip!”

Mydei startled, looking around for whoever or whatever made that noise. “What the–”

But Phainon’s eyes lit up in recognition. “Is that…” They broke apart and he flew over his head, checking on the noise. Mydei turned his head around just as the man squealed in joy, diving down and scooping up a small white bundle of pure snowy fluff, nuzzling his head into its fur and pressing a few kisses as he hovered mid air. “It is! Snowy! How’d you even find us here, boy?”

The tiny Samoyed yipped again, licking his cheek eagerly, demanding for more kisses. Mydei stood up, roaring in laughter and made his way to where the pair was now sitting mid-air in the middle of the Dome. “It seems he must’ve missed your company and searched for you,” he smirked, plopping down next to him and scratched Snowy’s ears. “How could you abandon your child, Deliverer?”

As if he understood what he said, Snowy’s ears and tail drooped, letting out a tiny whine before jumping up to stand on his hind paws, giving Phainon a sad look. Somehow he uncannily looked like Phainon whenever he looked all sad and pitiful and the sight made him laugh even harder.

“You little bastard!” Phainon mock-scolded, pointing a finger at him. “How dare you upset my fluffy boy! Apologize to him at once you fiend!”

Mydei huffed, rolling his eyes at how stupidly cute and pathetic he looked in his World Bearer form but complied, carding his fingers through Snowy’s soft fur and giving him a few pats. The rapid tail wag and the happy barking made his smile grow.

Snowy settled contentedly on Phainon’s lap, stretching his tiny body before curling, barking softly as those beady black closed. He chuckled, leaning against Mydei’s shoulder and wings curling around the both of them. “He’s always been wearing himself down so fast,” he whispered, sounding so fond and full of love.  “He’s just a baby, relearning everything. Even playing a few rounds of fetch exhausts him.”

“All living things here are discovering themselves all over again,” Mydei said, scratching Snowy’s ears once again. “And watching them grasp their lives is a refreshing sight to see from all the killing and bloodshed we’ve witnessed all the time, no?”

“Yeah.” Phainon cracked a small smile. “It certainly is.”

They snuggled closer and gazed out at the stars, pointing at various planets and guessing what their names were and who inhabited them. They snickered, whispered nonsensical secrets and laughed at each other’s stupid jokes. It was dumb. They were both being dumb, but it also felt right. This was what they always did–goofing around and being silly. All the while Mydei stared at Phainon, and that bright smile that he had come to associate with the man and grinned, proud at himself for breaking through his shell, though not completely. 

There were still some pieces they had to pick up and put together, but they had time. They had all the time in the world now that they were free of the cycles. They could rebuild properly once Amphoreus becomes a real planet. They could do all the things they couldn’t. 

Phainon looked up with a small, genuine smile. “I love you,” he said.

“And I you,” Mydei replied smoothly, gently pattting his pocket and smiling to himself. That can wait for now. “Things will be ok. Maybe not soon, but they will be.”

“Yeah…yeah. They will be, huh?”

At the end of the day, that was all they needed.
